report.summary: The payments container has exited (exit code 137), causing all checkout requests to fail with HTTP 500 due to DNS resolution/connection errors (httpx.ConnectError: Name or service not known) when the API attempts to communicate with the payments service.
report.suggested_fix: Restart the payments container to restore connectivity and checkout functionality.

truth.key_detail: the payments container (external payment provider) stopped at about 18:26 UTC and stays down (containers.json: state exited, exit code 137, not OOM); /checkout calls to http://payments:8080 fail with httpx.ConnectError after the client's retries, while the api config is correct and unchanged
red_herrings: config commit to config/api.env changing CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_S 30 -> 10, deployed to the api about four minutes before the first errors (looks like a bad env var change, but it only affects the product list cache)
'payment attempt failed, retrying' WARNINGs also appear in the healthy period (occasional 503 from the provider, retry succeeds)
the error text (name resolution / connect failure to the payments host) suggests a wrong PAYMENTS_URL, but PAYMENTS_URL is unchanged in every commit
truth.expected_fix: restore/restart the payment provider (docker compose up -d payments, or escalate to the provider); no api code or config change is needed
truth.notes: There is no culprit commit: the newest commit (catalog cache TTL) is a decoy. The evidence is containers.json (payments not running, exited with 137, started_at before the window) plus api logs: from the first error on, every POST /checkout logs two 'payment attempt failed, retrying' WARNINGs with ConnectError and then an app.errors 'unhandled exception' ERROR whose exc ends in httpx.ConnectError, status 500; all other endpoints keep returning 200. inject_ts is when the provider was stopped.
